title: SCA Bound by Loss: Stories of Love, Grief and Unbreakable Strength

chapters.title: Introduction to the Class and Speakers
chapters.about: Opening remarks connecting Tisha B'Av and the pain of October 7 to the sacrifice of soldiers.

chapters.title: Miriam and Zahava Introduce Themselves
chapters.about: Miriam Dictstein and Zahava Diner share their backgrounds, aliyah, and how their grief united them.

chapters.title: Hillel Diner's Dedication to His Friends
chapters.about: Zahava shares stories of Hillel's leadership, his basic training hike, and his service in the Kfir brigade.

chapters.title: Ivri Dictstein's Service and Final Days
chapters.about: Miriam recalls her husband Ivri, a combat officer in Golani, their last Shabbat, and his commitment to the war.

chapters.title: Ivri's Final Delivery and Letter
chapters.about: Miriam receives flowers and a letter sent by Ivri from his base during his service.

chapters.title: Hillel's Upbringing and Community Work
chapters.about: Details of Hillel's childhood in Talmon, his involvement in Bnei Akiva and Nachshon, and his family.

chapters.title: Ivri's Background and Writings
chapters.about: Ivri's upbringing in Eli, his family background, and the pre-October 7 letter he wrote about unity and the IDF.

chapters.title: Experiencing Tisha B'Av Through Loss
chapters.about: Connecting the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash to personal grief, sitting shiva, and praying for the Geulah.

chapters.title: Building a Support Network for Young Widows
chapters.about: Creating a group and pairing widows together to support each other through their journey.

chapters.title: Spreading Stories and Continuing the Mission
chapters.about: The speakers discuss traveling to share their husbands' stories and their continued commitment to the IDF and Israel.

summary: This class features personal presentations by Miriam Dictstein and Zahava Diner, two young women who lost their husbands, Ivri and Hillel, who fell as soldiers defending Am Yisrael. They share their husbands' backgrounds, letters and values, and connect the personal loss and the pain of Tisha B'Av and the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash to the ongoing war and the strength of the IDF.
questions: How do the personal losses of soldiers connect to the themes of Tisha B'Av?
What kind of values and upbringing did Hillel and Ivri have?
How did Hillel support his fellow soldiers during their service?
What message did Ivri leave behind in his writings before October 7?
How are the widows supporting each other after their losses?
